content.comment_body: As mentioned, the UDF folder does not appear in the file tree, and after spending a considerable amount of time searching online and exploring all program menus, I haven't found a solution. This prevents me from using my UDFs in the current project. I'm running [product_name] V7.0.30 in a new VirtualBox Windows 7 virtual machine. There were installation issues with Windows 10, so I'm using a virtual machine instead. Everything works fine except for the missing UDF folder, which may be unrelated. I have attached an image showing the file tree. Does anyone know what could be causing this?
The screenshot did not provide enough information. Did you specify the folder path for your UDF under the "Extras" menu after saving?
Yes, I set the path, but it didn’t affect the outcome. The UDF folder remains hidden, and the functions and instructions are missing from the file tree, as seen in my previous screenshot.
Please refer to the attached screenshot. I am not experiencing this issue, but I'm using Windows 7 and [product_name] V7.1.5.
If you look at your screenshot, you’ll notice that the "Data Log Profile" directory and the "Data Log" block are also missing.
In the first screenshot, the loaded program is named "BandSaw1.lsc". Which hardware is configured in this diagram? It seems that [product_name] [article_no] is not selected, correct?
That's correct, I missed checking for the data log folder. Nearly right about the hardware—it’s not the one you mentioned, it's [article_no]. I’m reusing an older device I received at no cost.

However, [product_name] [article_no] does not support UDF functionality. Only [product_name] [article_no] and [product_name] [article_no] offer this feature. The device you're using is an older model manufactured between 2003 and 2005 and has been discontinued.

That clears things up. I haven’t worked with this product before and have more experience using [version_no] series. This is just a small side project, reusing equipment previously removed from service. I remember the device ran a fuel oil pumping station about 4–5 years ago, so I didn't realize it was so outdated.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced difficulties accessing the UDF (User Defined Function) folder in [product_name] V7 when working with certain hardware. The issue stems from using an older, unsupported hardware version that does not allow for UDF usage. The software does not indicate this limitation clearly, resulting in confusion and time spent troubleshooting by users unfamiliar with these hardware restrictions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate the UDF feature will be consistently available and visible in the file tree, regardless of the hardware type selected, or at the very least expect clear notification about its availability or compatibility within the software.
